scope: Enumerate FUN_004DC690's high-switch (the `if (0x13D < uVar2)` branch covering opcodes 0x13E..0x1A8) and catalog every case body. Classify each case as Pattern A (receiver vtable[1] dispatch), Pattern B (actor vftable[9] generic dispatch), Pattern C (bespoke dedicated handler), or Pattern D (sub-dispatcher). Closes the Pattern C gap identified in docs/client-architecture.md, 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns' (~14 low-switch cases; high-switch unmapped).

method.step1: Read existing FUN_004DC690 decomp at %BCS_GHIDRA_PROJECTS%/fun_004dc690_decomp.txt (3364 bytes, BCS-Y-0279). Identified the `if (0x13D < uVar2)` branch and enumerated every case label from 0x13E to 0x1A8 inclusive.
method.step2: Cross-referenced every dedicated handler VA against manifests/symbols.json - NONE of the 47 unique handler VAs (FUN_0057xxxx + FUN_0055CF70 + FUN_00573F70 + FUN_00578C90 family) are currently cataloged.
method.step3: Batch-decompiled all 47 dedicated handlers via 3 Ghidra headless runs (handlers_batch1.txt 0x143..0x156 handlers, batch2.txt 0x16d..0x18b handlers, batch3.txt 0x18d..0x1a3 handlers). Output files at %BCS_GHIDRA_PROJECTS%/handlers_batch[1-3].txt.
method.step4: Classified each handler by structural pattern: thin C-trampolines (8-byte tail call to a worker) and 109-byte exception-wrapped FUN_00cc9320 lookups + worker call patterns are Pattern C; multi-case fallthrough to label switchD_004dc749_caseD_f at decomp line 756-760 uses Pattern B (FUN_004d9910 actor lookup + actor->vftable[9](zone_state)); case 0x193 (FUN_00578c90) is itself a switch dispatcher = Pattern D.
method.step5: Vtable-slot probe NOT applied - the handlers exhibit no `(**(code **)(*piVar + 0x4))(...)` shape that would indicate Pattern A receiver-class dispatch. All 47 dedicated handlers resolve to direct C-style worker calls (sometimes guarded by a FUN_00cc9320 manager lookup).

key_findings.title: Zero Pattern A receivers in the high switch - the s2c dispatch-pattern table needs correction
key_findings.detail: The dispatch-pattern table in docs/client-architecture.md, 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns' states 'High | if (0x13D < uVar2) | opcodes 0x13E..0x1A8 with case groups | Mostly *Receiver class dispatch (Pattern A)'. This enumeration finds ZERO Pattern A dispatches in the high switch. The actual distribution is 50 Pattern B (multi-case fallthrough to actor->vftable[9]), 44 Pattern C (bespoke per-opcode workers), 1 Pattern D (case 0x193 = FUN_00578c90 sub-dispatcher), 12 default-skip cases.
key_findings.implication: The 38-receiver receiver discovery pass catalog (Pattern A) must come from elsewhere - likely the low-switch via FUN_004D8860 sub-dispatcher (the pattern d subdispatcher pass has cataloged 27 Pattern A handlers there) and/or other dispatcher entry points the receiver discovery pass methodology walked. The correct characterization is 'Mixed Pattern B + C + D, no Pattern A'.

key_findings.title: High switch contributes 50 opcodes to Pattern B (actor vftable[9] generic dispatch)
key_findings.detail: BCS-Y-0527 currently lists only the 8 low-switch contributors (0x0F + 0xCC + 0xCD + 0xCE + 0xCF + 0xD0 + 0xD3..0xE5 partial). This enumeration covers 50 high-switch contributors that reach the same switchD_004dc749_caseD_f fallthrough label: 0x144, 0x145, 0x157..0x16C, 0x16F, 0x170, 0x175, 0x177, 0x179, 0x17B, 0x18E, 0x192, 0x194, 0x195, 0x197, 0x199..0x1A2, 0x1A4..0x1A8.
key_findings.implication: BCS-Y-0527's note should be expanded to list 58 total contributing opcodes (8 low + 50 high). Given the actor vftable9 investigation pass's finding that the cataloged actor classes' vftable[9] is a no-op, all 58 of these opcodes are effectively dropped at the dispatcher level (open question - see the Pattern B paragraph in docs/client-architecture.md, 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns').

key_findings.title: Pattern C handlers exhibit 3 structural shapes; the 109-byte manager-lookup family points to a shared subsystem
key_findings.detail: Shape (b) - 109-byte exception-wrapped FUN_00cc9320(*param_1) manager lookup + worker call - is shared by 14 high-switch cases (0x146 partial, 0x148..0x156, 0x16D, 0x176, 0x17C, 0x18F..0x191). FUN_00cc9320 reads *param_1 (the dispatcher's this pointer, which is a zone/session state pointer) and presumably returns a sub-manager pointer. FUN_00cc9330 is the symmetric cleanup. The 11 workers FUN_00580e70/ef0/f70/ff0 + FUN_005810xx/11xx/12xx/13xx/14xx/15xx form a strided VA family (0x80 apart, sequential opcodes 0x148..0x156) suggesting they live in a single source file - a 'CharacterState' or 'EntityStat' subsystem operating on a shared sub-manager type.
key_findings.implication: The 14 handlers in shape (b) and their 14 workers are likely a single subsystem (e.g., 'character stat update', 'inventory mutate', etc.). Cataloging the workers (FUN_005810xx etc.) as a unit + identifying FUN_00cc9320's return type would let us name the subsystem. A candidate for the catalog validation report pass.

key_findings.title: Opcode 0x193 is a Pattern D sub-dispatcher (FUN_00578c90, 842 bytes, 7 sub-cases)
key_findings.detail: Case 0x193 calls FUN_00578c90 which itself switches on the first packet payload arg (param_2 at +0x10). Sub-ops 0x10..0x16 have bespoke logic; sub-ops < 0x10 fall to FUN_0075f3e0. Sub-op 0x13 builds a string from sjis literals 'k0W0~0W0_0' and DAT_00fa6d5c/6d64/6d8c via FUN_00445cf0/0044ab90/0075bc90 chain - characteristic of chat or system-message packet formatting.
key_findings.implication: Opcode 0x193 multiplexes ~7 logical opcodes via its sub-op. The catalog should record the sub-op as a second-level dispatch key. Decompiling FUN_0075f3e0 + FUN_0075d2[1-7]0 would let us name each sub-op.

key_findings.title: Opcode 0x198 is a LGE name-registrar invocation point
key_findings.detail: FUN_00576150 calls FUN_00447260(payload, DAT_00f67298). FUN_00447260 is the LGE registrar chokepoint (compare BCS-Y-0521..0524 which catalog 8 LGE substrate functions that use the same FUN_00447260 + DAT_00f67298 pattern for _assignForChild and related ops).
key_findings.implication: Opcode 0x198 likely carries a Lua-class-name registration string from server to client (e.g., 'register this Lua class name on this actor'). Could bridge to Lua-class-system docs. A candidate for the catalog validation report pass to identify what string opcode 0x198's payload contains.

key_findings.title: Opcode 0x147 is observed-in-pcap-but-default-skipped, confirming Pattern E (docs/client-architecture.md, 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns')
key_findings.detail: 0x0147 InventorySetEndPacket has NO case body in the high switch - it falls into the default-skip path. This validates the earlier open-question status for 0x0147 in docs/client-architecture.md, 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns'.
key_findings.implication: Opcode 0x147 is not routed through FUN_004DC690. Its handler must live in a different dispatcher entry point (Lobby/Chat channel? c2s path?) - live capture capture deferred per project direction.
